chunks.arabic_text: حَمْدَوَيْهُ بْنُ نُصَيْرٍ، عَنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى، عَنِ الْحَنَنِ، عَنِ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ، عَنِ أَبِيهِ قَالَ

translations.en: Hamduwayh ibn Nusayr, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Hanan, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from his father who said:

chunks.arabic_text: دَخَلَ الْكُمَيْتُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ عَلَى أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ وَ أَنَا عِنْدَهُ، فَأَنْشَدَهُ مِنْ لِقَلْبٍ مُتَيِّمٍ مُسْتِهَامٍ، فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْهَا قَالَ لِلْكَمَيْتِ: لَا تَزَالُ مُؤَيَّدًا بِرُوحِ الْقُدُسِ مَا دَمْتَ تَقُولُ فِينَا

translations.en: Al-Kumayt ibn Zayd entered upon Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) while I was with him, and he recited to him [poetry] from 'A heart infatuated and ensnared', so when he had finished it, he said to al-Kumayt: You will not cease to be supported by the Holy Spirit as long as you speak about us.

en.summary: This hadith highlights the special status of al-Kumayt ibn Zayd, a prominent poet of the Imams, whose verses were considered a form of divine endorsement. Imam al-Sadiq’s promise of continuous support through the 'Holy Spirit' (Ruh al-Quds) underscores the spiritual authority granted to those who eloquently articulate the virtues of the Ahl al-Bayt. This connection between poetic praise and divine assistance reinforces the Shia tradition of valuing literary expression as a means of preserving and propagating Imamate identity.
en.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq promise the poet al-Kumayt ibn Zayd?

key_terms.الْكُمَيْتُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ: Al-Kumayt ibn Zayd, a famous poet known for his verses about the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ: Abi Ja'far, referring to Imam Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir or Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq
key_terms.رُوحِ الْقُدُسِ: The Holy Spirit (Gabriel), symbolizing divine inspiration and support
key_terms.مُسْتِهَامٍ: Ensnared or captivated, describing the state of the heart in love
